notes: The zip change is essentially the reference, but squashfs New now sets f.file from obj.Remote() computed under the old root, which likely breaks single-file roots in subdirectories.

The zip change is essentially the reference, but squashfs New now sets f.file from obj.Remote() computed before the root is adjusted, which likely breaks single-file roots in subdirectories (e.g. img.sqfs/dir/file.txt) for regular files too.

Clean, consistent implementation where List, NewObject and root all agree on the suffixed name, with good zip tests including escape and root cases; its only deviation is eagerly reading zip link targets at mount time.

Clean squashfs handling, and the root naming the suffixed link works like the reference, but zip symlink targets are read eagerly during readZip (extra I/O on remote archives), and the squashfs test depends on mksquashfs being installed.

Basic listing and lookup work, but the zip root-suffix trimming hack yields a bogus '.rclonelink' entry when root names a link, squashfs single-file roots on links are unsupported, it deletes an unrelated test doc comment, and there are no squashfs or escape tests.

Main listing, lookup and read paths work, but a zip root naming a link with the suffix produces a bogus ".rclonelink" entry, squashfs root detection for links isn't updated, the edit strips TestArchiveZip's existing doc comment, and the tests cover only zip.

Core list/lookup/open behaviour works, but roots naming a link require the raw name, the squashfs refactor with nil,nil returns and an allowRawLink flag is awkward, it includes unrelated comment edits, and only a basic zip test is added.

Squashfs NewObject("x.rclonelink") falls back to a regular file "x" and returns an object whose name the listing never shows, violating the List/NewObject agreement; the patch also churns unrelated comments and adds only a small zip test (no squashfs or hostile-archive coverage).

Core behaviour is correct and well tested (fixture, copy, escape), but roots must use the raw link name rather than the .rclonelink name, and it adds a link-only EOF special case and an unneeded readZip signature change.

Correctly skips links without --links, exposes them as .rclonelink with target content in both backends, keeps List and NewObject in agreement, and reads zip links lazily; however a root accepts the bare link name rather than the listed .rclonelink name, and the tests are strong (squashfs fixture, zip, copy and hostile-escape).

Correct for both zip and squashfs and handles suffixed roots and name collisions, but it heavily refactors readZip, eagerly decompresses every symlink at open time, and the squashfs root-candidate loop can resolve root 'x.rclonelink' to a regular file 'x'.

Functionally thorough (root with or without the suffix, collision handling with regular .rclonelink files, target size cap) and very well tested, but it heavily refactors readZip and eagerly opens every zip symlink at listing time, which costs extra remote reads on S3-hosted archives.
